literal: When the Zhou armies pressed close, he thereupon surrendered.
idiomatic: When the armies of Zhou closed in, he yielded.

literal: Posthumously granted Upper Opening Establishment and Governor of Yu Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted an upper opening establishment and the governorship of Yu Province.

literal: Lingshan, Governor of Changle, styled Jingsong, was a clansman younger brother of the Grand Ancestor.
idiomatic: Lingshan, Governor of Changle, styled Jingsong, was Gao Huan's clansman and younger brother.

literal: He followed the Grand Ancestor in raising troops at Xindu, and ended as Governor of Changle.
idiomatic: He followed Gao Huan when arms were raised at Xindu and ended his life as Governor of Changle.

literal: Posthumously granted Grand General and Minister of Works; his posthumous title was Wensuan.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made grand general and minister of works, with the posthumous title Wensuan.

literal: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan made Fuhu, son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's father's elder brother, successor to Lingshan's line.
idiomatic: His son Yi died as commander of the Wuping garrison without heirs; Emperor Wenxuan appointed Fuhu — son of Jianguo, Governor of Qi Province and Lingshan's father's elder brother — to carry on Lingshan's line.

literal: Fuhu, styled Chenyuan, had modest skill with brush and ledger.
idiomatic: Fuhu, styled Chenyuan, had some modest skill with brush and ledger.

literal: At the beginning of Tiantong he was successively promoted to Gentleman Attendant of the Yellow Gates.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiantong he rose through promotion to gentleman attendant at the yellow gates.

literal: Fuhu served through several reigns and always took part in confidential affairs, yet by nature he craved wine; in drunkenness he often blundered, and in his last years the habit grew worse still — for days he would take no food, doing nothing but drink until his mind wandered and he died.
idiomatic: Fuhu served several reigns and always stood in the circle of confidential counsel, yet wine was his weakness; drunk, he often stumbled, and toward the end the failing worsened — days passed without a meal, every hour given to the cup until his mind grew dim and he died.

literal: Posthumously granted Governor of Yan Province.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Yan Province.

literal: Yi, grandson of Marquis Jianguo, succeeded.
idiomatic: Yi, grandson of Marquis Jianguo, succeeded to the line.

literal: Yi in youth was careful and restrained.
idiomatic: From youth Yi was careful and restrained.

literal: At the end of Wuping he was Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gates.
idiomatic: At the end of the Wuping era he served as attendant gentleman at the yellow gates.

literal: In the Kaihuang era of Sui he was Vice Director of the Grand Treasury; he died by reason of an offense.
idiomatic: Under Sui in the Kaihuang era he served as vice director of the grand treasury and died having been convicted of an offense.

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
